title: Inveraray Watchtower Walk Route

images.title: Folly on Dun na Cuaiche by David Hawgood, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: The Dun Na Cuaiche tower is a folly, of a ruined watch tower, overlooking Inveraray and Loch Fyne. Built 1747-48 by William Douglas, at a contract price of £46 for the mason work, it was commissioned by the 3rd Duke of Argyll

images.title: View from Dun na Cuaiche by Steven Brown, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: View from Dun na Cuaiche

description: This walk takes you up to the wonderful viewpoint at Dùn na Cuaiche in the town of Inveraray. You can start the walk from the historic Inveraray Castle where there is a good sized car park. The route then follows gradually rising trails through the woodland to the tower. Here you can enjoy some wonderful views over Loch Fyne, the castle and the surrounding mountains. There's also the site of an ancient Iron Age Hillfort at the top.You can continue your walking in the area on theInveraray Forest Circular Walkwhich explores the woodland, ponds, and waterfalls to the north and west of the castle.
